children: A new peer-reviewed study from
published in

found that Medicare Advantage beneficiaries who used an integrated specialty pharmacy, which coordinates pharmacy services with a beneficiary’s health plan, experienced faster access to specialty medications and lower out-of-pocket pharmacy costs compared with beneficiaries using non-integrated specialty pharmacies. The research suggests
that greater coordination between health plans and specialty pharmacies can help improve the patient experience and make prescription drugs more accessible and affordable.

The study, conducted by Humana Healthcare Research, analyzed data from more than 23,000 Humana Medicare Advantage beneficiaries receiving specialty medications through CenterWell Specialty Pharmacy®. Specialty medications are typically more expensive than traditional prescription drugs and used to treat complex conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, HIV and osteoporosis. Researchers found that integrated specialty pharmacy care was associated with:
Nearly
six days faster access, on average,
to specialty medications compared with non-integrated specialty pharmacies.
Approximately
$106 lower annual out-of-pocket pharmacy costs
for beneficiaries compared to those using non-integrated specialty pharmacies.

The research also demonstrated that beneficiaries receiving care through a fully integrated model that incorporates primary care in addition to specialty pharmacy and the health plan led to approximately
$165 lower annual pharmacy costs
compared with beneficiaries using non-integrated specialty pharmacies.

“For people managing complex health conditions, waiting for a medication is the same as waiting to start treatment,” said Dr. Sanjay Shetty, President of CenterWell, Humana’s health services organization. “This research suggests that when pharmacy services, primary care providers and health plans work together more closely, patients can get the medications they need faster and at a lower cost."
